title: Recovery continuation evidence binding
description: Objective: close the J3 authority hole where caller-supplied release/handoff facts currently let ADOPTED, SUSPECT, QUARANTINED, and RECONCILIATION_COMMAND records gain successor authority. Deliverable: runner and daemon recovery contracts that derive and persist the exact predecessor-release fact and committed safe handoff from durable restart records, admit continuation only for the closed resumable classification set (ABSENT), and never trust those facts from the continuation request. NOT in scope: process killing, new crash classifications, doctor behavior, or canary tests. This is a shared runner/daemon wire-contract migration and must land producer and consumer together. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery/{recovery-contract.ts,crash-classification.ts,safe-boundary.ts,safe-boundary.test.ts}; apps/daemon/src/recovery/{restart-reconciliation.ts,restart-reconciliation.test.ts,continuation-contracts.ts,continuation-service.ts,continuation-service.test.ts,continuation-binding.test.ts}. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The runner derives release/handoff evidence from parsed restart records and exposes a frozen closed resumable-classification set containing only ABSENT; no caller field can manufacture either fact.

admitSuccessorOverlap/admitResume receive the durable classification/evidence and refuse each non-resumable classification with one stable recovery code at SAFE_BOUNDARY; an exhaustive five-class production-surface sweep asserts all five cases were generated.

ReconciliationRecord persists the exact derived predecessor release and safe handoff, and continuation reads those stored bytes instead of accepting predecessorRelease/safeHandoff authority from its request schema.

ABSENT with PROVEN_RELEASED plus a committed handoff appends one successor binding; ABSENT without that handoff and every other classification refuse with exact code/layer and leave the durable store byte-identical.
A hostile request carrying legacy or extra release/handoff assertions is rejected at the daemon ingress/continuation layer and cannot override the stored record.
The runner, daemon, and repo typecheck/test verification chain exits 0; the worker mutation-drills classification admission and stored-evidence sourcing, then commits only the owned paths.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

- `expected undefined to be 'PROVEN_RELEASED'` / `expected undefined to be 'handoff-stored-2'` — ReconciliationRecord does not carry the derived evidence yet (DoD 3).
- `expected 'CONTINUATION_REQUEST_SHAPE_INVALID' to be 'RECOVERY_CLASSIFICATION_NOT_RESUMABLE'` / `...to be 'RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN'` — the new no-authority request shape is not accepted yet.
- `expected 'REFUSED' to be 'REQUEST_INVALID'` — THE LIVE HOLE. A hostile request supplying its own `predecessorRelease: "PROVEN_RELEASED"` + `safeHandoff` against a record with NO stored handoff is accepted and reaches the boundary today. DoD 5 in one assertion.

THE AUTHORITY-BEARING BUILDER IS GONE FROM THE POSITIVE PATH. `continuation-test-harness.ts` is NOT an owned path, so I could not fix its `request()`. Instead both owned suites build their own request bytes locally with only the new fields, and the harness `run()` is imported ONCE under the honest name `legacyAuthorityRequest` and asserted to be REJECTED. The stale builder is now a hostile fixture rather than a trap. Its store/seed/snapshot/decision drivers are still used, as the plan allows.

ONE PLANNED ASSERTION WAS WRONG AND I REPLACED IT RATHER THAN STAGING IT. The plan implies keeping the ACTIVE/UNKNOWN release refusals as daemon cases. Once the release is DERIVED they are unreachable here: `heldResources` pushes `resource:<fact>` for any non-PROVEN_RELEASED, and quarantine is decided before absence, so an ABSENT record ALWAYS stores PROVEN_RELEASED. A test asserting RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_ACTIVE through continuation could only pass by staging a state the classifier cannot produce. Replaced with two honest tests: one proving a held resource classifies QUARANTINED and not ABSENT (refusing with the exact classification code), and one asserting every ABSENT record stores PROVEN_RELEASED — the tripwire that goes red if anything later decouples them and makes the lattice reachable again.

SWEEP IS NON-VACUOUS AND ORDER-SENSITIVE. `NOT_RESUMABLE` is hand-transcribed, asserted `toHaveLength(RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS.length - 1)` and `toBeGreaterThan(0)` before use; each case asserts the classification actually produced BEFORE asserting its refusal, and the union plus ABSENT is asserted equal to the full kind set. Each case also carries a `masked` code — the refusal its own stored release/handoff would produce if the classification gate were deleted — asserted via `not.toBe`. ADOPTED/SUSPECT/QUARANTINED mask RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_ACTIVE; RECONCILIATION_COMMAND masks RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN. A code-only assertion cannot catch gate deletion; these can.

Store byte-identity is snapshotted immediately before and after every refusal, and binding count is asserted 0 on each. The binding conflict case now uses a SECOND predecessor claiming the same successor (a different handoff can no longer come from the request), which exercises the real expectedVersion collision on the successor aggregate.

implementationPlan.description: Land producer and consumer together. Version the changed reconciliation-record and continuation-request schemas (use /2; leave the unchanged binding schema version alone). Add predecessorRelease and safeHandoff to ReconciliationRecord, fill them solely from CrashClassification's runner-derived evidence, serialize them into the durable record, and make decode/read validate the new exact values; legacy/incomplete records remain non-authoritative and cannot be upgraded optimistically. Remove predecessorRelease/safeHandoff from ContinuationRequest, REQUEST_KEYS, and parseContinuationRequest so legacy/extra assertions are rejected by the existing bounded exact-shape ingress. Narrow decoded binding classification to the runner vocabulary. In evaluateContinuationCommandBytes, retain unreconciled/unclassified gates, then pass record.classification, record.predecessorRelease, and record.safeHandoff to the two @moe/runner root functions; create the binding only from the admitted stored handoff. Preserve bindingTarget's aggregate+expectedVersion seam, byte-equal replay behavior, append-only writes, and exact runner/daemon refusal layers.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN, producer and consumer landed together. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` -> 34 files / 678 tests passed, exit 0. Runner unchanged and still 39 files / 1215 tests, exit 0. The 15 RED assertions from step 3 are green with none deleted, skipped or loosened.

WHAT CLOSED THE HOLE. `ContinuationRequest`, `REQUEST_KEYS` and `parseContinuationRequest` no longer DECLARE predecessorRelease/safeHandoff. Because the gate is exact-key, a request still carrying them is REJECTED on key count, not silently ignored — an implementation that merely stopped reading them would tell a hostile caller its continuation succeeded, which is a worse answer than a refusal. `evaluateContinuationCommandBytes` now passes `record.classification`, `record.predecessorRelease` and `record.safeHandoff` to both runner admissions; the request contributes only attemptRef/successorRef/identity.

SCHEMAS VERSIONED, LEGACY FAILS CLOSED. `moe-restart-reconciliation/2` and `moe-recovery-continuation-request/2`; the binding schema is untouched at /1 because its shape did not change. `decodeRecord` validates `predecessorRelease` against the runner's exported PREDECESSOR_RELEASES and `safeHandoff` as string|null, so a /1 row fails the version check, decodes to null, and is absent rather than upgraded — it can never reach continuation carrying a default.

BINDING CLASSIFICATION NARROWED. `ContinuationBinding.classification` is now `RecoveryOutcomeKind`, not `string`, and `decodeContinuationBinding` rejects anything outside that vocabulary. This matters because the RECONCILIATION vocabulary is one wider — it contains REFUSED — and a binding is by definition a record that some classification ADMITTED a resume. Added `isRecoveryOutcomeKind` as a real type guard so the admissions receive a narrowed kind with no cast.

REFUSED RECORDS GET UNKNOWN/null. The REFUSED arm carries no continuationEvidence, so its record stores predecessorRelease UNKNOWN and safeHandoff null — epic rail 4's honest pair, never a default toward release.

ONE OF MY OWN STEP-3 ASSERTIONS WAS WRONG AND I FIXED THE TEST, NOT THE CODE. The binding-conflict case asserted the whole durable store stays byte-identical. It does not, and should not: a rival predecessor claiming the same successor is a genuinely new command, so the store records it as `NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT` with EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT. That ledger row is exactly what makes retrying THAT command idempotent; asserting byte identity would have forbidden the idempotency record itself. The old test only passed because a same-attempt retry hits REPLAY and appends nothing. Replaced with the assertions that carry the actual meaning: exactly one non-committed row, on the successor aggregate; the winner's bindings byte-identical; still exactly one binding, still carrying the FIRST predecessor's handoff; and the loser's own reconciliation history unedited. This is pre-existing store behaviour my new two-predecessor case is the first to exercise — not a regression from this diff.

restart-reconciliation.test.ts needed NO edit: it reads the schema constant rather than the literal, so the /2 bump flowed through. All 184 recovery tests green.
